Definition: adverb from G1446; Hebraistically or in the Jewish (Chaldee) language:--in (the) Hebrew (tongue).
BiblicalUsage: Hebraisti means in the Hebrew tongue, and John uses it to name the places and words of Jerusalem. In John 5:2 there is a pool called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, in John 19:13 Pilate sits in the place called in the Hebrew tongue Gabbatha, and in John 19:20 the title on the cross was written in Hebrew and Greek and Latin.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe John names the Hebrew words because the story happened in a real place with a real language, and the cross stood at the meeting point of three worlds.
